findings.claim: --no-replace-objects does not disable a grafts file. git 2.55 still honours <GIT_DIR>/info/grafts; it prints a deprecation hint but uses it. A graft that re-parents the re-admission commit onto a backdated copy with the same tree makes blame attribute the line to the copy, so a re-admission committed after asOf passes the stale-floor refusal (serving-plan.ts:529). It is the same class of local state as replace refs and blame.ignoreRevsFile. git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository does not detect a grafts file. Measured neutraliser: GIT_GRAFT_FILE set to a non-existent path in the blame call's env restores the real attribution.
findings.counterexample: r6-x, re-admission X 2f8be022 (committed 2026-10-11T09:30:00Z), backdated copy Y a4d2841a (2026-10-02, same tree, parent X^). Replace ref deleted. Wrote X Y to .git/info/grafts. Plain blame: committer-time 1790899200. git --no-replace-objects blame: also 1790899200. rule serve floor.json --dry-run passes. GIT_GRAFT_FILE=<non-existent> git --no-replace-objects blame: committer-time 1791711000 (the real instant). With the grafts file present, rev-parse --git-path info/grafts returns .git/info/grafts and --is-shallow-repository returns false. FOLDED at 51368af4: the blame call runs with GIT_GRAFT_FILE set to a never-created path under os.tmpdir() for that call's environment only (serving-writer.ts:235, :271), the comment names the three neutralised states, a test writes the graft with a precondition on the re-dated blame and asserts the refusal with the real instant and nothing written (serving-writer.test.ts:988, RED on 788a552b), the changeset gains the clause; the r6-x graft probe re-run against the built CLI refuses naming 2f8be022 at 2026-10-11T09:30:00.000Z.
